# Payment Architecture

## Validation

- Validate the transaction
- Check compliance
- Execute payment

## System Performance Metrics

| Metric | Average | P99 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latency | 45ms | 120ms |
| Throughput | 1200 rps | 2500 rps |

> Note: All measurements were captured during peak traffic hours.

### Deployment Instructions

1. Pull the latest Docker container:
   ```bash
   docker pull registry.example.com/api/v2:latest
   ```
2. Run database migrations before starting the service.
3. Verify health check at `https://localhost:8080/health`.
**WARNING**: Modifying production environment variables will trigger an automated deployment pipeline. Refer to [Deployment Docs](https://docs.internal/deploy) for safety protocols.

# API Specification v3

This API uses *OAuth2* authentication. Provide your bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

`Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>`

- [x] Configure BPE tokenizer vocabulary
- [x] Train baseline transformer model
- [ ] Benchmark subword fragmentation on non-Latin scripts

### Added
- Support for multi-lingual subword tokenization
- Export metrics in CSV and JSON formats

### Fixed
- Resolved memory leak in asynchronous event processing loop

technical: The system uses asynchronous event-driven processing with idempotent consumers, distributed tracing and eventual consistency.
To mitigate high-frequency cache invalidation, the microservice layer implements a distributed LRU cache with write-through persistence and gossip protocol synchronization.
The multi-head self-attention mechanism computes Query, Key, and Value matrix projections using scaled dot-product attention with rotary position embeddings (RoPE).
By deploying zero-redundancy optimizer (ZeRO-3) partitioning, parameter memory footprint is distributed across 64 GPU worker nodes without sacrificing gradient communication bandwidth.
Database query latency was optimized by adding a composite B-tree index on `(tenant_id, created_at DESC)` and enabling parallel read replicas.
The API gateway handles TLS termination, rate limiting via token bucket algorithms, and dynamic request routing based on HTTP header inspection.
Quantization to INT4 precision using AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization) reduced model VRAM requirements by 65% with minimal perplexity degradation.
Kafka partition rebalancing triggers consumer re-assignment via cooperative sticky assignment strategy, minimizing partition revocation downtime.
The Kubernetes cluster utilizes horizontal pod autoscaling (HPA) governed by custom Prometheus metrics monitoring HTTP 5xx error rates and CPU queue depth.
Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) constructs subword vocabularies by iteratively merging the most frequent adjacent character byte sequences in corpus data.
